**Finding: deviation (WARRANTY) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I found:
- **§9 "TrueLink Warranties" (p0059–p0060)** is limited to a Y2K date-processing warranty — no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no services warranty, no malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and no remedy.
- **§11 Standard of Care (p0069)** requires only "the same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" — a self-referential standard of care, not a warranty with a remedy.
- **§12 disclaimer (p0076)** does carve out express warranties ("EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT"), so it doesn't swallow §9 — but there is little express warranty left to preserve. §3 hosting terms are "reasonable commercial efforts" obligations, not warranties.

Because there is no conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy at all, the document fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so this is a deviation rather than a fallback-compliant clause.

Redline: inserted a new paragraph after p0060 adding (i) professional and workmanlike services, (ii) 12-month conformance to documentation for the Interface and related software, (iii) no malicious code, (iv) compliance with laws — plus a re-performance/repair/replace/refund remedy, with the 90/30-day fallback flagged as negotiable in the comment.
